merge

MURJ (rhymes with urge) · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To join together and become one.

The two small streams merge into one river at the bottom of the hill.

Example

Our class will merge with Ms. Lee's class on the field trip, making one big group.

Two separate classes come together and act as a single group. When things join and become one, they merge.

How Strong Is It? — meet → merge → fuse

meet vs. merge

meet vs. merge: Meet is the milder word: things that meet touch but stay separate, while things that merge join together and become one, like two rivers flowing on as a single stream.

fuse vs. merge

fuse vs. merge: Fuse is the more complete joining: things that merge become one but might still be pulled apart, while things that fuse melt together so fully they can never be separated.

Put it together

Put it together: The whole word merge is the root, so there are no parts to peel away. Merge comes from a Latin word meaning 'to dip or sink.' You cannot see that old story in the word today, but the whole word still does the root's job all on its own.

Use the root in a new word: emerge

Use the root in a new word: emerge: We watched the turtle emerge from the pond and climb onto a warm rock.
